rationale: The candidate is coherent across views and the parcel containment appears satisfied, but it reads mainly as a compact wedge-on-podium with a stronger object character than a clearly public neighborhood building. The dominant gesture is legible and there is a modest hierarchy between the lower datum and upper wedge, yet the access edge response is weak: the thick blue frontage does not get a strong undercut, court, seam, or porch-like ground void. The silhouette is not incoherent, but the stepped/triangular upper form is only partially capacity-bearing and risks reading as an arbitrary roof wedge rather than a program-led section. Compared with the references, it has some resonance with courtyard/bridge/terrace precedents, but it underuses the most transferable principle: a meaningful carved public void tied to the street edge. Program-wise it can plausibly support neighborhood living only if the ground threshold is strengthened; as shown, it is marginal because the public edge and section logic are underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion/community-center than compact neighborhood-living; use the void/bridge logic, not the exact curvilinear roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise composed mass with a large carved central void and an upper bridge/readable threshold condition.
